title: Military government claims largest-ever drug lab seizures in northern Shan
detail: At a 25 January press briefing the military government said raids on 9-22 January at sites in Hsipaw and Mongyai townships seized about 2,343 kg of crystal meth ('ice') at one site, 12.4 kg of heroin and over 300 litres of liquid meth, valuing three main sites at K65.282 billion.
agency: Myanmar Police Force / Ministry of Information
attribution: Military-government claims by Maj-Gen Zaw Min Tun and Police Lt-Gen Win Zaw Moe; not independently verified

title: Air strikes kill at least 17 in Ponnagyun, Rakhine
detail: Military air strikes hit Yoengu village in Ponnagyun township, about 33 km northeast of Sittwe; at least 17 people including three children were reported killed and about 14-15 wounded, according to DVB and the Arakan Army.
attribution: Casualty figures per DVB and the Arakan Army as reported by Al Jazeera

title: Air strike on monastery sheltering displaced people in Katha
detail: The Irrawaddy reported a junta air strike on a monastery sheltering about 100 displaced people in Katha Township, killing around 80 including monks and children; it counted about 100 civilian air-strike deaths from 16-27 March after the new parliament opened.
attribution: Figures per The Irrawaddy citing local reports; not independently verified

title: Minbu opens heatwave shelters
detail: State media said Minbu Township authorities opened three daytime cooling shelters on 2 April for about 400 people, mainly elderly residents, amid extreme heat, with ministries donating K62.55 million in supplies.

title: Malaria surge in Chin, Kachin, Karenni, Sagaing, Tanintharyi
detail: The Myanmar Health Cluster reported a surge in malaria cases in endemic areas aggravated by a lack of insecticide-treated bednets, a seasonal dengue rise in Rakhine and Karenni, and high measles risk in Rakhine and Chin linked to an outbreak in Bangladesh.
attribution: Myanmar Health Cluster Bulletin, June 2026; no case counts given

title: Jade mine landslide in Hpakant: 5 dead, 15 missing
detail: A landslide at a jade mining area in Hpakant Township left five people confirmed dead and 15 missing, AFP reported via Myanmar Now.
attribution: AFP report carried by Myanmar Now

title: Thanlwin at Hpa-An and Shwegyin river above danger level
detail: Citing the Department of Meteorology and Hydrology, Moemaka reported the Thanlwin above danger level at Hpa-An, the Shwegyin above danger level and the Bilin at warning level; over 100,000 people were affected in Rakhine (Kyauktaw, Mrauk-U, Ponnagyun, Minbya) as of 11 July.
prov: Kayin State / Bago Region / Rakhine State
attribution: DMH river readings as reported by Moemaka

title: Floods hit 41 townships in one month
detail: ISP-Myanmar reported that floods between 10 July and 11 August 2026 affected 41 townships across Ayeyarwady, Rakhine, Sagaing, Mandalay and Bago, potentially affecting at least 1.3 million people.

title: Health Cluster reports cholera/AWD outbreaks in Yangon, Sittwe, Mon, Ayeyarwady
detail: The WHO-led Myanmar Health Cluster reported simultaneous cholera/acute watery diarrhoea outbreaks in Yangon, Sittwe, Mon and Ayeyarwady, plus AWD in flood areas of Sagaing, Mandalay and Bago; it also noted 101 attacks on health care from January to August 2026.

title: Yangon cholera: ~500 hospitalised, 150+ confirmed by mid-August
detail: BNI, citing Health Cluster and other data, reported nearly 500 hospitalisations and at least 150 confirmed cholera cases in Yangon by mid-August, with fatal cases in Yangon and Sittwe.
attribution: BNI citing WHO-coordinated Health Cluster and wire reports

title: GDACS: monsoon flood event, 15 dead and 10,493 displaced
detail: GDACS recorded a flood event from 4 July to 19 September 2026 with 15 deaths and 10,493 displaced, noting the Thanlwin (Salween) broke its banks in mid-August; it rated the event green (low humanitarian impact).

title: Arakan Army advances toward Sittwe from Ponnagyun
detail: Myanmar Now reported the Arakan Army said it seized three villages and advanced into junta-held Sittwe areas, including fighting at Min Chaung Bridge, while the military intensified drone attacks in northern Ponnagyun.
attribution: Arakan Army claims as reported by Myanmar Now

title: Shwe Kokko scam hub reported expanding again
detail: The Irrawaddy reported that scam operations at Shwe Kokko restarted from February 2026 after claimed 2025 demolitions, with new compounds and expansion into Kyaukphyar and Myawaddy wards 2 and 4; worker entry fees reportedly rose from 3,000 to 12,000 baht.
attribution: The Irrawaddy citing local sources and recruitment posts

title: Over 2,000 social media users arrested since coup, researchers say
detail: Data for Myanmar, cited by The Irrawaddy, counted 2,029 social media users arrested over five years since the 2021 coup (969 in Yangon and Mandalay), with 26 arrests for online dissent in 2026 through 31 August.
attribution: Data for Myanmar figures via The Irrawaddy

title: Chinese side fires warning shots as junta jets circle Laiza
detail: The KIA said shots were heard from the Chinese side as military aircraft flew toward its border headquarters at Laiza, which the aircraft had circled since 24 September; Laiza schools were closed for 1-2 weeks, and jets reportedly bombed KIA territory in Hpakant Township the same day.
attribution: KIA spokesperson and residents as reported by The Irrawaddy

title: Air and artillery strike on NUG Special Region Command HQ kills six
detail: The Irrawaddy reported military bombing and artillery shelling of the NUG's Special Region Command headquarters on the Kyaikto-Shwekyin border area, killing six including a prominent Air Force defector and injuring four including the command's head.
attribution: Casualty figures per resistance sources reported by The Irrawaddy
